## Long-form discussion (≤ 800 words)

**What it is.** Mem0 ("mem-zero", YC S24) is an Apache-2.0 memory layer for AI agents, distributed as `mem0ai` (PyPI/npm) and a hosted SaaS at `app.mem0.ai`. It claims a single goal: persistent, cross-tool, per-user memory that an agent can read and write through a small API surface (`memory.add(messages, user_id=...)`, `memory.search(query, filters=...)`). The OSS repo at commit `bd9d27ff` is a polyglot monorepo: Python SDK, TypeScript SDK, two CLIs, a FastAPI self-host server, the (now sunsetting) OpenMemory dashboard, an OpenClaw plugin, and a Claude-Code/Cursor/Codex plugin (`mem0-plugin/`).

**Architecture.** A write goes: `add(messages)` → LLM extracts facts using `ADDITIVE_EXTRACTION_PROMPT` (default `gpt-5-mini`) → entities are extracted via spaCy (`utils/entity_extraction.py`) → fact text is embedded (default `text-embedding-3-small`) → row written to a vector store + an entity collection + SQLite history. A read goes: `search(query)` → semantic top-k from vector store, BM25 keyword score over the same corpus, entity-match boost (`ENTITY_BOOST_WEIGHT` in `utils/scoring.py`) → fused via `score_and_rank` → optional reranker (Cohere / HuggingFace / LLM / SentenceTransformer / ZeroEntropy). 20+ vector backends are pluggable via `VectorStoreFactory`. The default local stack is Qdrant + SQLite history; the self-host server uses Postgres + pgvector.

**v2 → v3 algorithm change (April 2026).** The README documents a major break: "single-pass ADD-only extraction — one LLM call, no UPDATE/DELETE. Memories accumulate; nothing is overwritten." Crucially, **graph memory was removed**: prior versions supported Neo4j / Memgraph / Kuzu / Apache AGE / Neptune via `enable_graph: true`, with relations exposed on search results. v3 replaces the queryable graph with implicit "entity linking" — entities are still extracted and used as a retrieval-boost signal, but no traversable graph remains. This is a meaningful regression for users who depended on relationship queries; the migration guide explicitly warns to redesign.

**Benchmarks (cited).** From the v3 README table and `mem0.ai/research` (2026-04-25): LoCoMo 91.6 (vs. previous 71.4), LongMemEval 93.4 (+26 over v2's 67.8), BEAM-1M 64.1, BEAM-10M 48.6. Retrieval latency p50: 0.88s / 1.09s / 1.00s respectively. Mean tokens per retrieval: ~6.8–7.0K (versus ~25K for full-context). Historical numbers from the LLM.md and arXiv:2504.19413 paper: "+26% accuracy over OpenAI Memory on LOCOMO", "91% faster than full-context", "90% lower token usage". Baselines (OpenAI Memory, Zep, MemGPT) are not retabulated in the v3 page — the synthesizer should treat the v3 numbers as Mem0-vs-Mem0.

**Claude Code integration — strong.** Mem0 ships `mem0-plugin/` with a Claude Code marketplace entry (`/plugin install mem0@mem0-plugins`). It registers an MCP server at `https://mcp.mem0.ai/mcp` exposing 9 tools, plus lifecycle hooks (`SessionStart`, `UserPromptSubmit`, `PreCompact`, `Stop`, `SessionEnd`) for automatic capture and recall, and a `skills/mem0/` skill for SDK-mode. The OpenClaw plugin (`openclaw/`) is the same idea for OpenClaw agents. MCP-only install: `npx mcp-add --name mem0-mcp --type http --url https://mcp.mem0.ai/mcp --clients "claude code"`. Cursor, Codex, and Claude Cowork share the plugin.

**Differentiation vs. subject 08 (OpenBrain).** Both are Level 6 "single brain across tools". Mem0's identity is **LLM-extracted facts + multi-signal vector retrieval + plug-any-vector-store**. Its v3 stance is explicitly *append-only, no graph, retrieval-time entity boosting*. Where OpenBrain is expected to lean on a queryable structured store, Mem0 deliberately walked away from that direction in April 2026. Mem0 also has by far the broadest editor/agent integration matrix (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Cowork, OpenClaw, Vercel AI, LangGraph, CrewAI, AutoGen, browser extension).

**Hosted Platform variant.** Same SDK, replace `Memory()` with `MemoryClient(api_key=...)`. Tiers: Hobby free (10K add / 1K search per month), Starter $19, Pro $249, Enterprise custom (SSO, audit logs, on-prem). Lock-in is medium for Platform-only users (data export via `get_all` is available, but reranker/algorithm specifics are server-side).

**Risks / known limitations.** Non-deterministic extraction (LLM-dependent); no published write-latency p50/p95; graph traversal removed in v3 (breaking change); cross-tenant isolation is filter-level, not row-level; hosted Platform stores conversation content on Mem0 infrastructure.
